data.long_meaning: Anvay is a name derived from Sanskrit origin which means 'friend' or 'companion'. In Hindu mythology, Anvay is the name of Lord Krishna's childhood friend and loyal companion, Sudama. The name Anvay carries the meaning “Friend, Companion” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Anvay usually hope their child will grow to embody friend, companion and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Anvay was a prominent Jaina monk during the Gupta Empire (320-550 AD). He was a disciple of Haribhadra Suri and a teacher to Harishena, who is considered to be the author of the Harishena Prabandha Khanda of the Skandapurana. Anvay is known for his commentaries on various Jaina texts, including the Agamasudhakara, Tattvartha Sutra, and the Uttarardhakamaka.

Anvay is also mentioned in the 12th century Kannada literature as the author of the Anvayamaharabharata, a commentary on the Mahabharata. He is described as a scholar of both Jainism and Puranic Hinduism. Anvay's commentary on the Mahabharata is considered to be an important source of information on the historical context of the epic and its philosophical themes.
